entries.qa: Извините (eez-vee-NEE-tyeh) is equally common for a small apology; Простите is slightly more personal.
Не за что (NYEH-zah-shtah, lit. 'not for anything') is also very common in reply to thanks.
Lit. 'good'; the standard neutral agreement. Ладно (LAHD-nah) and Окей are also heard; Хорошо is the most neutral.
The number after на takes a collective/case form, not the plain number: на одного, на двоих, на троих, на четверых. See examples.
Back-translation: 'I have an allergy to ___' (lit. 'at me [is] allergy on ___'). The allergen takes the accusative case (на орехи, на молоко, на яйца). Gender-neutral.
Speaker gender: вегетарианец (man) / вегетарианка (woman).

Back-translation: 'Without ___, please.' Без takes the genitive: без мяса, без молока, без глютена, без льда, без орехов. For an allergy, pair it with 'У меня аллергия на ___' so staff know it is medical, not a preference.
Lit. 'Here, please'; the natural answer to 'Здесь или с собой?'. Fuller: Я буду есть здесь (I'll eat here).

один agrees with the item's gender: ещё одну for a feminine noun (чашку, бутылку, кружку пива), ещё одно for neuter (пиво, вино). Ещё один fits masculine items (чай, кофе, бокал). Reviewer: consider whether a neutral form is preferable.
До takes the genitive (до аэропорта, до вокзала). For trains/buses between cities, the city name also goes in the genitive: до Москвы.

Lit. 'Does this one go to ___?', said pointing at a bus or train (автобус, поезд, трамвай are masculine). For a commuter train (электричка, feminine) it would be Эта идёт до ___? To a driver: Вы едете до ___? (Are you going to ___?). Not sure which is best as a single default.

Lit. 'Drive me as far as ___, please' (taxi). До always takes the genitive. Отвезите меня в/на ___ is equally natural but its preposition changes per place (в аэропорт, на вокзал), so до was chosen to keep the frame fixed. In practice drivers also accept just 'До аэропорта, пожалуйста.'
следующий is masculine (поезд, автобус); for a feminine vehicle (электричка, маршрутка) use следующая.
At big long-distance stations the track is often called путь: Какой путь? (kah-KOY poot).
Lit. 'How much time to travel?'. Shorter Сколько ехать? is also common.

entries.qa: Direction 'to the left' (where to go). Location 'on the left' is слева (SLYEH-vah).
Direction 'to the right'. Location 'on the right' is справа (SPRAH-vah).
Speaker gender: заблудился (man) / заблудилась (woman).
Lit. 'Is it nearby?'. Это недалеко? (is it not far?) is equally common.
Lit. 'I have a booking'. бронь is the everyday word at hotels and restaurants; more formal: У меня забронирован номер (I have a room booked).
Wi-Fi is said 'вайфай' (vai-FAI) and often written in Latin letters.
Lit. 'At what time is departure?'. Hotels also say расчётный час (checkout hour): Во сколько расчётный час?
Lit. 'Can I leave luggage here?'. Вещи (things) is also used: Можно оставить здесь вещи?
Plural subjects take не работают. For hot water the natural sentence is Нет горячей воды (There is no hot water), used in the examples instead of the frame.
Беру! (bee-ROO, 'I'm taking it') is a shorter everyday alternative.
пакет = shop bag (plastic or paper); shops often charge a few roubles for it.
Lit. 'Cut my hair, please'. Мне нужна стрижка (I need a haircut) is also fine.
Lit. 'Just even it up'; the usual way to ask for a trim.
Lit. 'Like in the photo', said while showing it. Вот так (vot TAHK, 'like this') also works. [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]
Back-translation: 'Help!' (lit. 'help [me]!', polite/plural imperative). The standard shout for help.
Back-translation: 'Call the police!' (вызвать = summon). Emergency number 112; police direct 102.
Back-translation: 'I need a doctor' (lit. 'to me [is] needed a doctor'). Gender-neutral. For an ambulance: Вызовите скорую! (Call an ambulance!), number 103 or 112.
Back-translation: 'Where is [the] pharmacy?'. For the nearest one: Где ближайшая аптека?
Back-translation: 'It's urgent!'. This is the everyday way to say it; Это экстренный случай (it's an emergency case) is more formal and less often shouted. [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]
Back-translation: 'I lost ___.' Speaker gender: потерял (man) / потеряла (woman). The object takes the accusative (паспорт, сумку). Russian normally omits 'my' here.
Back-translation: 'I feel bad (unwell)' (lit. 'I badly myself feel'). Gender-neutral. Shorter and more urgent: Мне плохо (I feel sick/faint). The first в in чувствую is silent.
Back-translation: 'I need to make a phone call' (lit. 'to me [it is] necessary to call'). Add Можно с вашего телефона? to ask to use someone's phone. [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]
Lit. 'At you is there ___?'. The noun stays in the nominative, so the blank takes the plain word.
Plural items take стоят (STOH-yaht): Сколько стоят билеты?

Back-translation: 'To me [is] needed ___, please.' The word for 'needed' agrees with the noun (нужен masc., нужна fem., нужно neut., нужны plural), so it is inside the blank: Мне нужна помощь, Мне нужно такси. Gender-neutral for the speaker. Safety: 'I need help' = Мне нужна помощь (lit. 'to me [is] needed help'); shouted, Помогите! (Help!). 'I need a doctor' = Мне нужен врач (lit. 'to me [is] needed a doctor').
Lit. 'Here nearby is there ___?'. Noun stays nominative. Тут поблизости есть ___? is equally common.
Lit. 'Can [one] pay ___?'. The means of payment goes in the instrumental with no preposition (наличными, картой, телефоном), so 'with' is inside the blank. Matches the vetted Можно оплатить картой?
Lit. 'Can [you] ___, please?' + infinitive; matches the vetted Можете повторить? / Можете мне помочь?

Lit. 'For me ___ without ___, please' (the usual way to order; gender-neutral, unlike Я бы хотел/хотела). First blank is accusative (воду, кофе, чай), second is genitive after без (молока, сахара, льда), so case changes are inside the blanks.
Lit. 'Is it allowed here to ___?' + infinitive; same pattern as the vetted Можно оставить здесь багаж?
The object takes the accusative (feminine nouns change: гостиницу), so the case form is inside the blank. Gender-neutral.

Lit. 'Does ___ go into the price?'. Chosen over ___ включён? because включён/включена/включено/включены changes with the noun's gender; входит only changes for plural (входят). Not sure which a native would pick as the default; both are common.
Lit. 'Where is it possible to ___?' + infinitive. Gender-neutral.
Said to someone you are flirting with; both gender forms are shown where the language changes with who you talk to.

how_much_is.qa: номер = hotel room. Per night: Сколько стоит номер за ночь?

i_need.qa: Back-translation: 'To me [is] needed help.' пожалуйста dropped: it sounds odd in an urgent request. In real danger shout Помогите!
To ask for some to drink, Дайте, пожалуйста, воды (Give me some water, please) is more usual.
такси is neuter, hence нужно. Asking staff to order one: Вызовите мне такси, пожалуйста (Call me a taxi).

pay_with.qa: Lit. 'pay by phone'; Russian omits 'my'. Note: foreign-issued cards and phone wallets generally don't work in Russia, so cash may be the real answer.

can_you.qa: Lit. 'Can you write this, please?'. Shorter and just as polite: Напишите, пожалуйста (nah-pee-SHEE-tyeh).

can_i_here.qa: For a free seat people usually ask Здесь свободно? (zdyes svah-BOD-nah, 'Is it free here?').

looking_for.qa: свою = 'my own' (accusative); отель (ah-TEL, masc.: свой отель) is also common for hotels.
Где вход? (Where is the entrance?) is what most people would actually say.

is_included.qa: Hotels equally say Завтрак включён? (ZAHF-trak fklyoo-CHYON).
Russian shelf prices normally include VAT (НДС), so this is rarely asked; a tourist/hotel tax would be туристический налог.
For a flight ticket, Багаж включён в билет? (Is luggage included in the ticket?) is more specific.

where_can_i.qa: Lit. 'Where can one take a taxi?'. In Russian cities taxis are mostly ordered by app (Яндекс Go).
Foreigners need a passport to buy a SIM in Russia.
